ep.doubles.s1.text: And 6 more, just like a mirror! 6 plus 6 is 12.

ep.doubles.s2.text: Near doubles are one more. 6 plus 7 is the double, and 1 more...

ep.make-ten.s3.text: Plus 9 is plus 10, then 1 back. 5 plus 10 is 15...

ep.bridge-ten.s0.text: 8 plus 5. 8 cookies in one tin, and 5 in the other.

ep.doubles-back.s1.text: Take one row away: 7 are left. 14 take away 7 is 7!

ep.doubles-back.s3.text: The ten goes, the 6 stay. 16 take away 10 is 6!

ep.ten-back.s2.text: Take away 9? Take away 10 first: 15 take away 10 is 5...

ep.ten-back.s3.text: ...then give 1 back: 6. So 15 take away 9 is 6!

ep.think-plus.s0.text: 13 take away 5? Turn it around: 5 plus what makes 13?

ep.zero-one.s2.text: Times 0 means zero groups. 5 times 0: no groups of 5 at all...

ep.times-2.s0.text: 6 times 2 means 2 groups of 6. Here is one group.

ep.times-2.s1.text: And the second group: it is a double! 6 plus 6 is 12.

ep.times-2.s2.text: Turn it round and it is the same: 2 times 6 is 12 too.

ep.times-10.s0.text: 4 times 10 means 4 sticks of ten blocks.

ep.times-5.s2.text: Half of 60 is 30. So 6 times 5 is 30!

ep.times-4.s0.text: 3 times 4. Start with one row of 3.

ep.think-times.s0.text: 12 divided by 3 means share 12 into 3 groups.

ep.think-times.s3.text: Think times: 4 times 3 is 12, so 12 divided by 3 is 4.

ep.dec-tenths.s1.text: One piece is one tenth. We write it one over ten, or zero point one.
ep.dec-tenths.s1.why: first take started loud and read 'it' as 'at'

ep.dec-tenths.s2.text: Three pieces are three tenths: zero point three.
ep.dec-tenths.s2.why: first take read 0.3 as 'zeroed on three'

ep.dec-hundredths.s0.text: One hundred squares make one whole. One square is one over one hundred, or zero point zero one.

ep.dec-hundredths.s2.text: Three rows and five more squares: thirty-five hundredths, zero point three five.

ep.alg-two-step.s0.text: Two x plus one equals seven. Two boxes and a weight on this side, seven weights on that side.
ep.alg-two-step.s0.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-order.intro.text: The Comet Cat wrote three, plus two times four. Which part do we do first?
ep.alg-order.intro.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-letters.intro.text: In the Star Lab, a letter is a box with a number inside. What is three n, when n is four?
ep.alg-letters.intro.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-letters.s0.text: Three n means three times n: three boxes, with n inside each one.
ep.alg-letters.s0.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-gather.intro.text: The Comet Cat packed three bags, each with a box and two weights. That's three lots of x plus two.
ep.alg-gather.intro.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-gather.s0.text: Three, bracket, x plus two: three groups, each a box and two weights.
ep.alg-gather.s0.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-gather.s2.text: Three boxes and six weights. So three lots of x plus two is three x plus six: the three times everything inside!
ep.alg-gather.s2.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-ineq.intro.text: The Comet Cat wants a number bigger than three. x is more than three. Which numbers work?
ep.alg-ineq.intro.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words

ep.alg-ineq.s0.text: x, greater than three, means x is more than three.
ep.alg-ineq.s0.why: math signs and letters read aloud in words
